burning-city-map.png.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: finished vertically scrolling background map for a premium 16-bit helicopter arcade shooter. This is a production map texture, NOT a mockup, screenshot, tile sheet or poster.
Canvas: very tall portrait 1024 x 3072, aspect ratio 1:3. Fill every pixel, opaque.
View: strict straight-down orthographic bird's-eye view, no horizon, no sky, no perspective convergence, no isometric angle.
Scene: a contemporary city devastated by a spreading explosion. The player will fly from the BOTTOM of this image toward the TOP, seeing a different neighborhood every few seconds. Make the entire long map unique, with no repeated blocks or identical buildings. Two fairly continuous north/south asphalt boulevards at about 27% and 73% of the width, 8-10% wide, form readable routes through the devastation. Side streets and intersections vary naturally. Roads remain clearly legible under scattered debris.
Bottom third: bombed residential and commercial blocks, roofless brick apartments with visible interior rooms, shattered corner shops, collapsed parking garage, scorched empty lots and burnt-out small cars.
Middle third: a distinctive broken circular civic plaza and crater, smashed multi-story office shells, collapsed floors, long exposed beams, heaps of concrete slabs and twisted rebar spilling onto the sidewalks. A destroyed elevated cross-street overpass with fallen spans and wrecked vehicles.
Top third: devastated industrial district approaching a freeway, gutted warehouses, broken sawtooth roofs, ruptured storage tanks, larger fire-blackened factories.
Destruction must be unmistakable: irregular shattered silhouettes, exposed rooms, fractured roofs, piled rubble of visibly different sizes, dusty impact streaks, cracked asphalt, crater rims, hanging steel skeletons, charred trees. Some intact rooftop fragments establish contrast and scale.
FIRE: throughout all three sections, include several small but unmistakably luminous pools of orange-red embers and concentrated golden flame cores amid the rubble, surrounded by black scorch. Keep fires localized to specific destroyed buildings and burning vehicles, not a border. NO tall smoke plumes baked into the map; these will animate in the game. NO atmospheric haze hiding the detailed ground.
Style: beautifully crafted late-16-bit / Neo Geo arcade PIXEL ART. Crisp purposeful pixel clusters, textured materials, fine structural detail, convincing height from short coherent building shadows, readable silhouettes. Muted soot slate blue, weathered concrete gray, dusty brick and brown rust; hot orange and yellow fire is the strong accent. No smooth vector rectangles, no generic repeated box buildings, no identical roof grids, no photorealism, no painterly blur. Moderate-dark environment so military enemies and bright bullets stand out; preserve lots of useful detail in shadows.
No helicopter, no live tanks, no enemy units, no projectiles, no interface, no lettering, no titles, no logos, no watermark. Stationary tiny abandoned wrecks are okay. All landmarks stay naturally integrated into one continuous city map.
